common_name: Premium Sun Coral Candy Coleus (AAS-Winning First Seed Coleus National Winner)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, pressing the fine seed onto the mix surface since light aids germination; Coral Candy tolerates full sun far better than older seed coleus strains.

directions: Start the fine seed indoors on the surface of moist mix, since it needs light to germinate, then transplant into full sun or partial shade after the last frost. Premium Sun Coral Candy was the first seed-grown coleus ever to earn an AAS National Award, prized for narrow, serrated leaves splashed in pink, burgundy, and green on a uniformly compact, mounded plant that keeps its color even in full-sun exposure that fades many older coleus strains. Pinch the growing tips and remove any flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant bushy and focused on foliage rather than bloom. A large container planted with three seedlings fills in quickly into a dense, colorful mound for patio or bedding display.
sources: All-America Selections — Coleus Premium Sun Coral Candy 2023 National Winner announcement

common_name: DoubleShot Orange Bicolor Snapdragon (AAS-Winning Double-Flowered Bicolor Snapdragon)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, surface-sowing since the fine seed needs light to germinate, and set out hardened seedlings around the last frost; DoubleShot is an intermediate-height, open-faced double snapdragon well suited to both beds and cutting.

directions: Start seed indoors on the surface of moist mix, since light is needed for germination, and transplant into full sun once seedlings are hardened off. DoubleShot Orange Bicolor is an AAS-winning snapdragon bred for open-faced, fully double flowers rather than the traditional hinged snapdragon face, opening warm orange and softening toward dusty rose-pink as they age, all carried on sturdy, well-branched stems. The strong branching habit produces more flowering stems than typical snapdragons, extending the display and giving plenty of length for cutting. Snapdragons perform best in cool weather, so plant out early and pinch young plants once to encourage additional flowering stems; deadhead or cut spent spikes to keep the plant productive into summer.
sources: All-America Selections — Snapdragon DoubleShot Orange Bicolor F1 2023 National Winner announcement

common_name: Blue by You Salvia (AAS-Winning Early-Blooming Perennial Meadow Sage)
scientific_name: Salvia nemorosa x pratensis 'Blue by You'

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring or fall into well-drained soil in full sun; Blue by You is a sterile hybrid salvia that puts its energy into a longer, earlier bloom season rather than seed production.

directions: Plant container-grown starts in well-drained soil in full sun, in spring or fall. Blue by You is an AAS-winning perennial salvia, a hybrid between Salvia nemorosa and S. pratensis, that opens its rich blue flower spikes up to two weeks earlier than comparison varieties and, being sterile, reblooms repeatedly through the season rather than slowing down once it sets seed. The dense, well-branched habit stays tidy without staking and shrugs off summer heat and drought once established, drawing bees and other pollinators over a long bloom window. Shear the plant back by about a third after each flush of bloom to trigger a fresh round of flower spikes, and expect reliable winter hardiness through USDA zone 4.
sources: All-America Selections — Salvia Blue by You 2023 National Winner announcement

common_name: Burning Embers Celosia (AAS-Winning Bronze-Foliage Plumed Celosia)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost, or direct sow once soil is warm; Burning Embers is a compact plumed celosia whose bronze, dark-pink-veined foliage adds color even before the plumes open.

directions: Start seed indoors at warm soil temperature and transplant, or direct sow, into full sun once the soil has warmed. Burning Embers is an AAS-winning plumed celosia notable for bronze foliage patterned with dark pink veins beneath vivid pink flower plumes, giving the compact, low-branching plant two-tone color appeal even before it fully flowers. Judges noted it produced the largest and longest-lasting plumes among trial comparisons, and it keeps flowering steadily through heat and humidity that can stall other bedding celosia. Deadhead spent plumes to tidy the display, and avoid overwatering since celosia is prone to root rot in soggy soil; established plants are quite drought tolerant.

common_name: Big EEZE Pink Batik Geranium (AAS-Winning Interspecific Mosaic-Patterned Geranium)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants after the last frost into full to partial sun; Big EEZE Pink Batik is an interspecific geranium that combines the heat tolerance of ivy geranium parentage with an upright zonal-type habit.

directions: Plant nursery starts after frost danger has passed into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Big EEZE Pink Batik is an AAS-winning interspecific geranium that crosses the heat resilience of trailing ivy geranium into a classic upright zonal habit, producing large 4-5 inch flower heads over 100 blooms strong, splashed with a mosaic of dark pink over lighter pink petals. The dark green foliage stays clean and the plant holds its shape without the legginess some zonal geraniums develop by midsummer. Deadhead spent flower heads to keep bloom coming from spring through frost, and treat as a warm-season annual outside zones 9-11, where it may persist as a tender perennial.

common_name: Solarscape XL Pink Jewel Impatiens (AAS-Winning Sun-and-Shade Interspecific Impatiens)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost at warm soil temperature and transplant after frost danger has passed; Solarscape performs in both full sun and shade and carries strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew.

directions: Start seed indoors at warm soil temperature and transplant into beds or containers after the last frost, in sun or shade alike. Solarscape XL Pink Jewel is an AAS-winning interspecific impatiens bred for a dense, mounded habit and satiny, pearlescent pink flowers up to 2.75 inches across, with strong resistance to the impatiens downy mildew that devastated traditional Impatiens walleriana plantings. Its adaptability across light conditions, from full sun to fairly deep shade, makes it a flexible mass-planting choice for beds, borders, and mixed containers. Keep soil evenly moist, since impatiens wilt quickly in dry conditions, and expect continuous bloom from planting through the first frost without deadheading.

common_name: Siam Gold Marigold (AAS-Winning Tall Golden African Marigold)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost, or direct sow once soil has warmed; Siam Gold is a tall African marigold reaching 24-30 inches, well suited to the back of a bed or as a cut flower.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost, or transplant started seedlings, into well-drained soil in full sun. Siam Gold is an AAS-winning African marigold bearing large, densely double, globe-shaped golden-yellow blooms 3-4 inches across on tall, uniform, well-branched plants, giving a strong vertical presence in beds or cutting gardens. Its sturdy stems hold flowers well above the foliage, making the blooms easy to cut for arrangements or to dry. Marigolds thrive in lean soil without heavy feeding, which favors flowers over foliage; deadhead spent blooms regularly to keep the tall plants flowering continuously through the season.

common_name: EnViva Pink Petchoa (AAS-Winning Mounding Petunia-Calibrachoa Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant nursery starts after the last frost into full sun; EnViva Pink is an intergeneric Petunia-Calibrachoa hybrid with a well-controlled mounded habit suited to containers and hanging baskets.

directions: Plant nursery-grown starts into well-drained, fertile soil or a quality container mix in full sun after frost danger has passed. Its large, bright pink flowers with a yellow throat bloom heavily from spring through fall and bounce back quickly after heavy rain, unlike many trailing petunias that need constant grooming. Its drought tolerance and low, spreading form make it a strong choice for edging, groundcover, and hot, sunny spots where taller annuals struggle, and it draws butterflies and bees throughout the season. common_name: Sure Shot White Petunia (AAS-Winning Compact No-Deadhead Petunia)

planting.note: Plant nursery starts after the last frost into full sun; Sure Shot White is a compact, mounding petunia that stays under a foot tall and needs no deadheading.

directions: Plant nursery-grown transplants into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun once frost danger has passed. Sure Shot White, an AAS Great Lakes regional winner, produces fragrant, 2-3 inch pure white flowers over green foliage on a naturally compact, mounding plant that stays tidy without pinching or deadheading, since spent blooms drop cleanly on their own. It suits containers, garden beds, and hanging baskets equally well and holds up to wind and rain better than many trailing petunia types.
